title: Testing graph expansion

problem.name: Testing graph expansion
problem.statement_latex:
For a bounded-degree graph, distinguish expansion at least $\Phi$ from being $\varepsilon$-far from every graph with expansion at least a specified smaller threshold $\Phi'$. The gap between $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ is part of the testing promise. Expansion controls mixing and the robustness of cuts.
Complexity counts neighbor queries and quantum or classical operations implementing the prescribed random-walk tester.
problem.statement_text: For a bounded-degree graph, distinguish expansion at least $\Phi$ from being $\varepsilon$-far from every graph with expansion at least a specified smaller threshold $\Phi'$. The gap between $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ is part of the testing promise. Expansion controls mixing and the robustness of cuts. Complexity counts neighbor queries and quantum or classical operations implementing the prescribed random-walk tester.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{1/3}/\Phi)$, Apers\textquotesingle s fast-forwarding and seed-set tester.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n^{1/3}/\Phi)$, Apers's fast-forwarding and seed-set tester.
quantum.details_latex: The proximity parameter and degree are fixed. The promise relates the accepting expansion threshold $\Phi$ to the smaller rejecting threshold as specified in the tester theorem. The bound combines an evolving-set construction with quantum fast-forwarding and estimates of the resulting walk distribution.
quantum.details_text: The proximity parameter and degree are fixed. The promise relates the accepting expansion threshold $\Phi$ to the smaller rejecting threshold as specified in the tester theorem. The bound combines an evolving-set construction with quantum fast-forwarding and estimates of the resulting walk distribution.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(\sqrt n/\Phi^2)$, classical random-walk expansion testing; $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ queries at fixed parameters.
classical.headline_text: $\widetilde O(\sqrt n/\Phi^2)$, classical random-walk expansion testing; $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ queries at fixed parameters.
classical.details_latex: The classical algorithm checks whether sampled walk endpoints exhibit the concentration expected in poorly expanding regions. Upper and lower bounds refer to bounded-degree oracle access with the stated gap between the two expansion thresholds.
classical.details_text: The classical algorithm checks whether sampled walk endpoints exhibit the concentration expected in poorly expanding regions. Upper and lower bounds refer to bounded-degree oracle access with the stated gap between the two expansion thresholds.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial in $n$, and quadratic improvement in the walk-time dependence $\Phi^{-2}\to\Phi^{-1}$. The mechanism is quantum fast-forwarding and amplitude estimation.
strength.description_text: Polynomial in $n$, and quadratic improvement in the walk-time dependence $\Phi^{-2}\to\Phi^{-1}$. The mechanism is quantum fast-forwarding and amplitude estimation.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous oracle advantage for the testing promise.
evidence.description_text: Rigorous oracle advantage for the testing promise.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant coherent walk steps require logarithmic vertex registers, seed-set storage and estimation ancillas. The seed-set data structure supports coherent access; total depth depends on $\Phi^{-1}$ and the target confidence.
